notes.title: Remastered edition of Home is Where One Starts..., now available
notes.notes:
Surprise! For the past few months, I've been working on a major update for my first game, Home is Where One Starts.... I made this short, exploration title in 2015 to prove to myself I could finish a project, and it honestly did better than I anticipated (I wasn't expecting much, haha). It inspired me to make a new game that was slightly larger called The First Tree, and that release [url=https://youtu.be/Y3Rs1z7it5M]changed my life[/url]. I wanted to make sure this small game was up-to-date so future players could play it on their system without any legacy crash problems.

There are countless updates, but here are the biggest one:
[list]
[*]64-bit engine upgrade (helps with compatibility on all systems, especially MacOS)
[*]Input system totally revamped. All controllers should work.
[*]Added a run button! Whaaattt??
[*]Huge graphical overhaul
[*]Changed the objective of the game due to confusion. Now, it's simply "Find the 8 memories"
[*]Added a familiar creature from The First Tree (can you find it?)
[*]Countless bug fixes, performance optimizations, and quality of life improvements
[/list]

I'm normally not one to work on old projects... I'd rather move on and make something new and better. But this imperfect game holds a special place in my heart since it inspired The First Tree, so I hope you enjoy this new improved version. Thanks for all your support, and now go find some memories!

- David

notes.title: My new game The First Tree is now out!
notes.notes:
In case you missed, you can now play The First Tree, a beautiful 3rd-person exploration game about a fox looking for her missing cubs, while at the same time she uncovers a second story about a son reconnecting with his father in Alaska.

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8546192/419e6556c53f16d12469e7468f4a0b2e3834c80c.gif[/img]

Here's a link to the [url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/555150/The_First_Tree/]store page[/url]. I think you'll find that the game has more in common with Home is Where One Starts... than you might think. ;)

notes.title: Celebration + New Game Announcement
notes.notes:
I’m happy to announce that [i]Home is Where One Starts...[/i] was nominated for the [url=http://www.emotionalgamesawards.com/nominees.html]Emotional Game Awards[/url] alongside indie juggernauts like [i]Life is Strange[/i] and [i]Ori and the Blind Forest[/i]. It didn’t win, but just being nominated was an honor. To celebrate, my game is 80% off for a week. Thanks again for all the support and the sales! These profits will help me fund my next project, which leads me to this...

I’m working on a new story-driven game: [url=www.thefirsttree.com]The First Tree[/url]. You can learn more and sign up for a one-time release email on the game’s website, www.thefirsttree.com. In this game, you play as a fox looking for her missing family while learning about a young couple dealing with a death in theirs. If you’re fan of [i]HiWOS[/i] and other games like [i]Journey, Firewatch,[/i] or [i]Brothers: a Tale of Two Sons[/i], I think you’ll like this one. Follow me on [url=http://twitter.com/DavidWehle]Twitter[/url] for more updates. Thanks again!

notes.title: Big update for Home is Where One Starts...
notes.notes:
I thought it would be fitting with school starting up again to release an update for [i]Home is Where One Starts...[/i] (and a big discount to boot). The big updates include Linux 64-bit support, subtitles (which can be easily edited for fan translations), Steam Trading Cards, and a huge variety of small fixes and additions.

Please note that the Linux version is still in beta, and you can visit [url=http://steamcommunity.com/app/355970/discussions/0/520518053448061855/]this forum post[/url] on potential compatibility issues. Also, if you’re interested in creating a fan translation of the game, visit [url=http://steamcommunity.com/app/355970/discussions/0/520518053448074171/]this post[/url] about the subtitle system to learn more.

Thanks again for everyone’s support! It’s been a great journey sharing this small story with everyone, and your kind words do not go unnoticed. By the way, I believe there is still an ending no one has discovered yet! I look forward to seeing if you guys figure it out. If something is on your mind, feel free to send me an email at homeiswhereonestarts@gmail.com .
